The relevant paths show: Rinderpest points to Wildebeest, with a negative sign beside the arrow; Wildebeest points to Grass, with a negative sign beside the arrow; Grass points to Fire, with a positive sign beside the arrow; Fire points to Trees, with a negative sign beside the arrow. The figure also shows other nodes such as Humans, Elephants, Rainfall, etc., but the question focuses on the indirect path from Rinderpest to Trees. Reasoning: propagate the influence along the directed chain Rinderpest -- negative --> Wildebeest -- negative --> Grass -- positive --> Fire -- negative --> Trees. Increasing rinderpest will decrease wildebeest; a decrease in wildebeest will cause grass to increase; an increase in grass will cause fire to increase; an increase in fire will decrease tree numbers. Therefore, the most reasonable prediction of the indirect effect of increasing rinderpest is that the number of trees decreases.

method.method_draft: First describe the figure as a causal model with signed arrows. Trace the directed chain from Rinderpest to Trees: Rinderpest -- negative --> Wildebeest -- negative --> Grass -- positive --> Fire -- negative --> Trees. Propagate an increase in rinderpest through the signs: more rinderpest lowers wildebeest; fewer wildebeest raises grass; more grass raises fire; more fire lowers tree numbers. Conclude that increasing rinderpest could indirectly lower tree numbers.
